Senses.Explanation: The organized call for the whole community's shared labor. The term occurs 1,567 times in 282 allowed texts. The monastic regulations define it directly: 'the rule of the general work summons is that upper and lower share the labor equally' (普請之法蓋上下均力也). The same section says that when work requires the assembly's combined strength, the administrators report it, inform the head monk and disciplinarian, and hang the general-summons placard (報眾掛普請牌); at the wooden-fish or drum signal, those not exempted go together to the work site. Encounter records name the labor. Baizhang returns from a summons to open fields and Huangbo calls it 'the assembly monks doing work' (普請開田；眾僧作務). Nanquan asks the disciplinarian what today's summons will do and receives the answer 'pull the mill' (今日普請作甚麼。對曰。拽磨). Dongshan inspects the quarters during a summons and finds a resident who did not attend. A lamp record depicts an unnamed resident hoeing during the summons when the meal drum sounds, and another records a summons to pick tea (普請摘茶). Other recurrent activities include hoeing, sorting vegetables or bracken, carrying firewood, planting rice, and planting trees. The word names the all-community summons and its work.
Senses.Note: The direct regulations definition is supported by early lamp and encounter records. The formula 'during the general work summons' occurs 96 times in 51 texts, 'attend the general work summons' nine times in nine texts, and 'go out for the general work summons' six times in five texts. No competing self-definition was found. Figurative invitations to the assembly to look are deployment extensions, not a separate sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 普請之法蓋上下均力也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Revised Baizhang Monastic Code (勅修百丈清規), redacted by Dehui: the regulations directly define the general work summons as upper and lower sharing the labor equally.

Occurrences.Kwic: 分付堂司行者報眾掛普請牌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Revised Baizhang Monastic Code (勅修百丈清規), redacted by Dehui: the regulations tell the hall attendant to notify the assembly and hang the general-summons placard.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師囙普請開田回問運闍梨開田不易檗云眾僧作務
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in Baizhang Huaihai's record: Baizhang asks Huangbo Xiyun about returning from a general summons to open fields, and Huangbo answers that the assembly monks were working. Responsibility is keyed to Baizhang as the containing master.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), spoken by Nanquan Puyuan in his explicit section: Nanquan asks the disciplinarian what the day's summons will do and is told that it will pull the mill.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師因普請次。巡寮去。見一僧不赴普請。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dongshan Wuben of Yunzhou (筠州洞山悟本禪師語錄), concerning Dongshan Liangjie: the record narrates his inspection of the quarters during a general summons and his finding a monk who did not attend.

Occurrences.Kwic: 因普請钁地次。忽有一僧。聞飯鼓鳴舉起钁頭大笑便歸。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), in Baizhang Huaihai's explicit section: Baizhang is responsible for the narrated case of a monk hoeing during the work summons when the meal drum sounds.
Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), in Guishan Lingyou's explicit section: Guishan is responsible for the tea-picking summons and the ensuing exchange with Yangshan Huiji.

Senses.PreferredTarget: a call for everyone to look
Senses.Explanation: A public call inviting everyone to look. In the recurrent formula, named hall speakers say to beat the drum and call everyone to look, then point the assembly toward lamps, the moon, the visible world, or the matter just raised. Dahui Zonggao uses it during the first full moon after lighting several lamps; Chushi Fanqi follows it with 'pierce through the eye'; and Juelang Daosheng places it between a stone blooming and the great earth dancing. Here the headword names an invitation to collective looking, not the monastery's organized labor call.
Senses.Note: The formula meaning 'call everyone to look' occurs 181 times in 101 allowlisted texts. Its requested act and immediate objects differ from the institutional work summons, so item 8 requires a second sense rather than treating it as a figurative reading of labor.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今朝正月半。有則舊公案。點起數盌燈。打鼓普請看。看即不無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄), full-moon hall address. Dahui Zonggao is the exact speaker who lights several lamps, says to beat the drum and call everyone to look, and then asks what happens when the lamps go out.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今朝正月半，燈月光撩亂，目前無一物，打鼓普請看。復云：刺破眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi (楚石梵琦禪師語錄), Lantern Festival hall address. Chushi Fanqi is the exact speaker who says to beat the drum and call everyone to look, then adds, 'Pierce through the eye.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸佛出身處，石上好栽花；打鼓普請看，大地舞婆娑。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Juelang Daosheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師語錄), hall address. Juelang Daosheng is the exact speaker who says that flowers can be planted on stone, calls everyone to look, and says the great earth dances.
